author.name: Horace Chan
author.headline: Expert in applying AI in verification

text:
Hardware engineer's job is pretty safe from AI.

I just ran an experiment, I asked Opus-5 to recreate 74181 in SystemVerilog from the original spec pdf one-shot. It just has to write an implementation plan, a testplan, a formal plan, then write a UVM testbench, run the simulation, write the assertions and prove them, close the coverage, pretty easy task, even an intern can do it.

Opus has been running for 2 hours, burning almost $200 tokens and there is no ending in sight.

The funny thing is during my feasibility research, Opus said it already know 74181 from its weight. It can answer questions about 74181 pretty well.

comments.text: hmm, I wouldn't take this as proof that hardware engineers are "safe". Models will get much better at RTL and verification flows. The harder part is that hardware doesn't forgive "mostly right". You can generate something that looks clean, simulates for a few cases, and still miss a corner case, synthesis behavior, timing assumption, or physical constraint that shows up much later. Imo, AI will definitely speed up the loop. But in silicon, the cost of being confidently wrong is not a bad deploy. It is a respin.

author.name: Kevin Normoyle
author.headline: Life!

comments.text: Two interpretations to clarify before I start: Behavioral — model the 74181's function (ALU operations, carry, equals) without worrying about gate-level structure. Structural/gate-level — replicate the actual logic gates as close to the original chip as possible.

author.name: Kevin Normoyle
author.headline: Life!

replies.text: I got something right away in sonnet 4.6 so you have to describe more what you asked for, and why it was a problem. It's not a problem: 74181 ALU in SystemVerilog — behavioral model with full pin-accurate I/O. Dual-mode: logic (bitwise ops) and arithmetic (add/subtract variants), selected by M. All 16 function combinations per mode driven by S[3:0]. Carry is active-low throughout, matching real chip convention. Includes group lookahead outputs (G, P) for chaining with a 74182, and AeqB for comparisons. Clean always_comb block — no clocks, no state, pure combinational.

author.name: Kevin Normoyle
author.headline: Life!

replies.text: my first iteration had some issues, but easily fixed ❌ What's Missing b_eff declared but unused — dead code, and it'll cause a compile error in context. No testbench — with the arithmetic bugs above, there's no way to catch them without one. Active-low input variant — there are two truth tables: active high data and active low data. The same circuit can be represented as though the outputs are inverted or not. Your file only handles active-high. A parameter or second module for active-low would be needed for a complete model. AeqB open-collector behavior — the A=B pin is wired as low or tri-state rather than low or high. Your model drives it as a normal logic output. For accurate silicon modeling it should be wire with tri-state (1'bz when false). No overflow/signed flag — not on the original chip either, but commonly needed when integrating.

author.name: Dave Rich
author.headline: Distinguished Technical Advisor at Arteris IP DVCon Technical and Steering Committee SystemVerilog IEEE Technical Chair

comments.text: People did similar experiments when RTL synthesis tools were first introduced. A gate-level hardware engineer would take a single-page RTL specification and generate a significantly more efficient gate design than a synthesis tool could. Youu could spend a considerable amount of time constraining the synthesis tool and allowing it to perform more optimizations.The engineer would say, "Why Bother?" Eventually, the number of RTL lines of code grew so much that a gate-level engineer could no longer design the individual gates themselves, leading to synthesis tools winning over. All those gate-level design engineers became RTL design engineers.

replies.text: Horace Chan It's exactly the same path. Digital gate logic replaced analog switches; register transfer logic replaced gates. IP blocks are replacing RTL. But it's never 100% replacement either because of legacy or secret sauce.
